details:
Project Overview

Space Explorer is an interactive web application that helps people explore astronomical images from NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Our prototype processes a SPHEREx FITS observation and displays it in a browser-based viewer, where users can zoom, pan, adjust brightness and contrast, and explore different color representations.

Scientific Approach

SPHEREx observes the sky in near-infrared wavelengths, providing scientific data that helps researchers investigate galaxies, stars, and interstellar material. Our team worked with astronomical image data and observation metadata to understand how scientific observations are stored, interpreted, and visualized. We also explored the challenges involved in finding observations of the same region of the sky at different times, including coordinate matching, image overlap, and instrumental noise.

Technology and Engineering

We used Python and astronomical data-processing and visualization tools, including Astropy and Plotly, to inspect and present the data. We built an interactive HTML experience so users can explore the image without needing specialized astronomy software. We focused on making the controls understandable while preserving useful scientific context.

Impact and Future Development

Space Explorer bridges scientific computing and public engagement by making NASA’s SPHEREx data easier to explore through interactive visualization. We aim to help students, educators, and astronomy enthusiasts connect with real infrared observations and discover how scientists study the universe. Future development will focus on searching additional observations, comparing images across different times, and expanding scientific analysis capabilities.

AI Assistance

AI tools assisted our development process with coding suggestions, debugging, and writing support. Our team reviewed and adapted the resulting work while developing and testing the application.
